feedback: Written before this candidate has raced, so no outcome is stated for it. The geometry you propose is the iteration 5 set, which I am keeping. Iteration 5 (score 52.36) and iteration 4 (score 52.20) show the outer reach and footprint are neutral; iteration 3 vs 2 showed the 0.14 m / 0.6 kg body cut s-bend progress from 0.16 to 0.1275, so the body stays. Iteration 6 kept your geometry and raised kd from 0.15 to 0.25, lifting the score to 97.7 with oval progress 0.40 and slalom progress 0.153, but slalom rms rose to 0.0333 and line loss to 1.35. So the geometry is not the limit on progress; the controller damping is. This round I raise kd to 0.35 on the same geometry. If the next race shows progress rising with rms and oscillation holding, the geometry is sufficient and you should keep it. If slalom line loss stays at 1 or more with progress still near 0.15, the untested geometry lever is wheel_track.
requested_changes: Keep sensor_positions at x = +/-0.036 and y = 0.04, sensor_size 0.016, and the 0.18 m / 0.8 kg body. Evidence: iteration 5 (score 52.36) and iteration 6 (score 97.7, same geometry) are the best-supported layout, and the body change at iteration 2 cost about 6 points.

If slalom line_loss_events stays at 1 or more and slalom progress stays below 0.16 after the damping change: test wheel_track 0.14 (from 0.12), changing nothing else. Evidence: iterations 3 to 6 never changed the turn rate per wheel, and slalom line loss has stayed at 1 or above across all of them.
Do not change body_length or mass again. Evidence: iteration 2 (0.14 m, 0.6 kg) cut s-bend progress from 0.16 to 0.1275, and iteration 3 recovered it to 0.16 on the baseline body.
